generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n    \n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n    \n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n        \n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n        \n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n            \n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            \n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Calculate Euclidean distance between two points\ninline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return < min_diameter) {\n            min_diameter = max_dist;\n            closest_point = candidate;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return closest_point;\n}\n\n// Generate a candidate cluster starting from a                                   threshold, N, \n                                                       &candidate_members);\n            \n            if (cardinality > max_cardinality) {\n                max_cardinality = cardinality;\n                best_seed = seed;\n                best_cluster_members = candidate_members;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // If we found a ++step) {\n                // Block-wide argmin and live-candidate count\n#pragma unroll\n                for (int off = 16; off > 0; off >>= 1) {\n                    const double ov = __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, bv, off);\n                    const int oi = __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, bi, off);\n                    const int op = __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, bp, off);\n                    if (ov < bv || (ov == bv && oi < bi)) { bv = ov; Distances use the same fused multiply-add the original build uses, and ties are broken the same way.\n- **No unnecessary recomputation.** I proved that removing points outside a seed's cluster leaves that cluster unchanged. So results are cached and a seed is recomputed only when one of its own members was removed. Upper bounds on cluster size let most seeds be skipped without changing which cluster wins.\n- **CUDA:** one thread block builds one seed's cluster. Distance checks are screened in single precision with a safe margin, and the exact double-precision calculation runs only when the result could change. This matters because the 3090 is very slow at double precision.\n- **MPI:** one GPU per rank. Large batches of seeds are split across ranks and the results gathered. Small batches are computed on every rank, avoiding communication delay.\n- **OpenMP:** the host-side bookkeeping, with thread counts scaled to the amount of work.\n\n**Things to know**\n- **Building:** `CMakeLists.txt` now needs CMake 3.24 or newer and compiles GPU code for the GPUs of the build machine. If you build on a node without a GPU, pass `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86` (or your GPUs' architecture). It also passes `-ffp-contract=fast`, which is required for the generated points to be bit-identical to the original.\n- **Small N hangs:** with N below about 30 the program hangs in data generation.
